headline: DiscoveryRSI paper reports iterative gains in evidence-bounded hypothesis development
summary: The authors introduce DiscoveryRSI, which develops linked research hypotheses and investigation plans, then learns from scored research histories through model training, workflow replay and new investigations. In four life-science domains, they report automated hypothesis-quality scores rising from 4.86 for the base model to 5.39 after two rounds. A blinded human review of 292 proposals by 27 biomedical or clinical research participants reports improved revision scores, while the paper’s literature-correspondence comparison is descriptive and sensitive to retrieval coverage. Results are author-reported; no independent reproduction or scientific outcome is established.
